t: The Umayyads turned the caliphate into a hereditary monarchy ruled from Damascus, from 661 to 750.
Their conquests reached from Spain to Sind and Central Asia. They spread Arabic and prepared the ground for Islam across three continents.
Favouring Arabs over non-Arab converts bred revolt; the Abbasids overthrew them in 750, though a survivor founded a new Umayyad state in Spain.
dyk: Abd al-Malik's gold dinar of 697 dropped Byzantine and Persian imagery for Arabic Quranic inscriptions, creating a distinctly Islamic coinage.
ev: Muawiyah secures the caliphate after Ali's assassination and rules from Damascus
Husayn ibn Ali is killed at Karbala, the defining martyrdom of Shia Islam
Abd al-Malik completes the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem
Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses into Spain and overthrows the Visigothic kingdom
The second Arab siege of Constantinople begins and fails the following year
Charles Martel checks Umayyad raids at the Battle of Tours
Abu Muslim proclaims the Abbasid Revolution in Khorasan
Marwan II is defeated at the Great Zab and killed, ending Umayyad rule in the east
